Maria: quick thought — the quickstart launcher CTA in the top-right + the ephemeral checklist snackbar is causing a keyboard focus loop for screen reader users. noticed when I tabbed through the page it never reaches the workspace picker. :thinking:
Dylan: ugh, ok. can you repro steps? is the snackbar grabbing focus on open?
Maria: yep — snackbar gets role=alert and focus is moved to it via JS so keyboard lands there, but the launcher is still tabbable. once snackbar appears, shift+tab/Tab seems to loop between launcher and snackbar.
Sam: screenshots or a short recording would help. which browser/AT?
Maria: chrome + NVDA (but saw similar in VoiceOver on mac). repro script: open onboarding page, press launcher, wait for quickstart banner -> snackbar appears after sample import, try tabbing.
Kevin: quick alternative is to not move focus to the snackbar and rely on aria-live announcements instead. snackbar can be announced via aria-live="polite" and keep focus flow intact.
Dylan: design-wise, we also need to decide if the launcher should be inert while checklist/snackbar is visible. disabling the launcher while the checklist is active might be simpler. But that feels like hiding a primary CTA.
Elaine: from accessibility POV, moving focus is fine if it's to a modal dialog. For non-modal snackbars, it's better to use aria-live and not steal focus.
Maria: agree re: modal vs non-modal. Our snackbar isn't modal. so aria-live is better. but we also need to handle keyboard users who expect to see / interact with the checklist items (keyboard-checklist).
Sam: what if we change snackbar to a dismissible inline banner in the header area with `role="status"` and a focusable "View checklist" link? That keeps everything in DOM order and gives keyboard access.
Dylan: that could work. Visually similar to snackbar but persists until dismissed. We'll need copy tweaks — shorter line + CTA: "View setup checklist" vs "Open quickstart".
Maria: copy suggestion: "Setup checklist ready — review steps" (primary CTA: "Open checklist"). Keep it 50 chars max for small screens.
Kevin: implementation note: use `aria-live="polite"` on the banner container, no focus override, and make the CTA the only programmatic focus after it appears if we want to draw attention (i.e., call focus() on the CTA but only for sighted keyboard users?). That gets tricky. I'd avoid programmatic focus unless it's a modal.
Elaine: +1 avoid programmatic focus. Instead ensure the banner is inserted in the DOM right after the main header so it becomes visible in sequential navigation. Also ensure color contrast >= 4.5:1 for CTA on busy backgrounds.
Sam: quick code sketch for the announcement approach:
```
// insert banner node with role=status and aria-live=polite
const banner = document.createElement('div');
banner.setAttribute('role', 'status');
banner.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
// append after header so sequential focus will encounter it naturally
header.parentNode.insertBefore(banner, header.nextSibling);
```
Dylan: thanks — that should help engineers. For design: make the banner height compact (40px), include an inline "x" dismiss. Also provide a keyboard-only visible focus ring.
Maria: a11y nit: ensure the dismiss button has aria-label="Dismiss setup banner" and is focusable.
Kevin: also guard against multiple banners stacking if import events fire twice — debounce event for 5s.
Sam: should we also add a telemetry flag to track keyboard focus flows for this surface? e.g., event when user tabs into the banner and when they open checklist.
Elaine: yes capture events but keep PII-free. those metrics will tell us if keyboard users find the banner useful.
Dylan: next steps: design mock for inline banner + copy variation A/B ("Open checklist" vs "View steps"), engineering to prototype with aria-live approach and no focus stealing, product to run a short keyboard/AT test.
Maria: assigning follow-ups: @Dylan to update mocks, @Sam to prototype, @Kevin to add debounce + aria implementation, @Elaine to write test plan. I'll do accessibility validation after the prototype.

Dylan: got it, starting mock now. will post Figma link soon.
Sam: I'll try to get a working prototype by EOD tomorrow and include NVDA/VoiceOver notes.
Kevin: I'll add the debounce and aria attributes, and a unit test for banner insertion order.
Elaine: drafting a 5-step keyboard/AT checklist for QA and will share in #help once ready.
Maria: thanks all — this feels like a small surface but good to settle the focus flow now. :thumbsup:
